\section{Gaussian Space --- Boolean Blocks}

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Boolean Blocks: Introduction}
Finite coordinate reindexing and currying preserve product measures. The Boolean Bobkov inequality therefore holds for arbitrary finite coordinate sets and for arrays of bits.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Boolean Blocks: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Currying preserves finite product measures]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_finiteCurry}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $I,J$ be finite sets, and let $B$ be a measurable space with measurable singletons.
For each $i\in I$ and $j\in J$, let $\mu_{ij}$ be a sigma-finite measure on $B$. The
currying bijection from arrays indexed by $I\times J$ to $I$-indexed arrays of
$J$-indexed arrays sends the product measure with coordinate measures $\mu_{ij}$ to the
iterated product measure that first groups coordinates by $i$ and then by $j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bobkov inequality for finite coordinates]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_inequality_finite_index}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_inequality, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_uniformBool_pi_eq_expect, BooleanAnalysis.derivative, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{6}
Let $I$ be a finite set and let $f:\{0,1\}^I\to\mathbb R$ take values in $[0,1]$. Under
independent uniform bits, define $D_i
f(x)=\bigl(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})-f(x^{i\leftarrow1})\bigr)/2$, where $x^{i\leftarrow b}$
sets coordinate $i$ to $b$. Then $\overline I(\mathbb E f)\le\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline
I(f)^2+\sum_{i\in I}(D_i f)^2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bobkov inequality for Boolean arrays]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_inequality_array}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_inequality_finite_index, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_finiteCurry}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ and $J$ be finite sets and let $f:\{0,1\}^{I\times J}\to\mathbb R$ take values
in $[0,1]$. Under independent uniform bits, let $\mathbb E f$ denote its expectation and
define $D_{ij}f(x)=\bigl(f(x^{ij\leftarrow0})-f(x^{ij\leftarrow1})\bigr)/2$, where
$x^{ij\leftarrow b}$ is obtained by setting coordinate $(i,j)$ to $b$. Then $\overline
I(\mathbb E f)\le\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f)^2+\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in
J}(D_{ij}f)^2}$.
\end{lemma}
